title: Depth-first traversal — Directory Tree Traverser
description: DFS descends each branch fully before backtracking, using a stack (or recursion). It needs memory proportional to tree depth, not tree size. DFS suits 'find the first match down this path' exploration.

title: Breadth-first traversal — Directory Tree Traverser
description: BFS visits level by level using a queue, finding the shallowest matches first. Its memory grows with tree width, which can be large. BFS suits 'find the nearest match' queries.

title: Cycle-safe traversal — Directory Tree Traverser
description: Symlinks and mounts can cycle; traversers track visited (device, inode) pairs to avoid infinite loops. Revisited directories are reported once and skipped. Cycle safety is mandatory on real filesystems.

title: Pruning subtrees — Directory Tree Traverser
description: Pruners skip branches by name pattern ('.git', 'node_modules') or by predicate. Skipping early avoids descending into huge irrelevant subtrees. Pruning is the biggest traversal speedup in practice.

title: Parallel traversal — Directory Tree Traverser
